abstract: A karyotypically normal male embryonal carcinoma (EC) cell line, P19, produced large numbers of chimaeras in midgestation after groups of cells were injected into mouse blastocysts. A wide variety of apparently normal tissues were colonized by the EC cells but most chimaeras were also morphologically abnormal. Few live chimaeras were produced and all contained tumours of EC cell origin as well as EC contributions to normal tissues. This apparently incomplete regulation of the EC cells by the embryonic environment was not due to EC cell variation, since a clonal subline. P19S18, produced similar patterns of colonization. It was also not caused by the inability of the blastocyst to regulate large numbers of injected EC cells, since a single P19S18 cell could contribute to both normal and tumour tissue in the same mouse. Neither a high rate of colonization of the embryo nor a normal karyotype is, therefore, sufficient to ensure reversion of EC cells to normal embryonic behaviour.
abstract_ja: 核型が正常な雄性胎児性癌（EC）細胞株P19は、マウス胚盤胞に細胞群を注入した後、妊娠中期に多数のキメラを生じた。多くの正常組織にEC細胞が定着したが、ほとんどのキメラは形態的に異常で、いずれにもEC細胞由来の腫瘍が含まれていた。生存するキメラは少数だった。この不完全な制御は、EC細胞の変異によるものではなかった。クローン亜株P19S18も同様の定着パターンを示したためである。また、胚盤胞が大量のEC細胞を制御できないことが原因でもなかった。単一のP19S18細胞が正常組織と腫瘍組織の両方に寄与したからである。したがって、正常な核型も高い胚への定着も、EC細胞が正常な胚様挙動へ復帰することを保証するには不十分である。
